page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled (2 threads per core) running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The CPU includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache, with support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2 instruction sets. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the ecs.u1-c1m1.2xlarge in the average performance tier across most standardized tests. It achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1856.99 and a multi-core score of 7723.84. Memory bandwidth tests show 424.69 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 59.61 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 42.56 GB/sec for large-block writes. In application-specific benchmarks, the instance handles static web serving at 9.4 GB/sec and processes 7.86 million Redis SET operations per second. However, compute limitations are evident in machine learning tasks; while it manages 169.25 tokens/sec for text generation on a small 135M LLM, performance drops to a weak 7.76 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.u1-c1m1.2xlarge is its highly constrained memory capacity relative to its 8 vCPUs. This 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks that require multi-threaded processing without high memory overhead, but renders it unsuitable for memory-intensive applications or large-scale database hosting. The lack of local storage also necessitates reliance on network-attached storage. This instance is best fit for workloads such as lightweight web serving, software compilation, text processing, and basic multi-threaded utility tasks.
